title: CIF Ancient Systems Test Series (incorporating The Giza Transmission Hypothesis)
description: Eight disciplined, fully-cited case studies that stress-test the Coherent Inheritance Framework (CIF) against real archaeological and historical evidence of knowledge transmission, loss, and survival across deep time: the Giza pyramids, Aboriginal oral traditions, the Antikythera Mechanism, the Late Bronze Age Collapse, Japanese tsunami stones, Polynesian wayfinding, Gobekli Tepe, and undeciphered scripts. Each study is written to be falsifiable, separates established fact from inference and speculation, and ends with a shared verdict taxonomy and a mandatory falsification check. The series includes the framework document, a cross-disciplinary polymath grading review, and a capstone synthesis. CIF is a candidate cross-domain framework (formerly Unified Inheritance Physics, UIP); it is offered as a structured vocabulary and set of design propositions, not as established physics.
notes: Series release 2.0.2 (patch release: source archive cleaned of a non-content platform system file; no changes to intellectual content vs. 2.0.1). Concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21618895 (latest). The foundational Giza case study was previously published at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21618896. Source: https://github.com/derekhone/cif-ancient-systems-test-series.
